# V47 reference builds: complete choice maps and independent expectations

Preparation artifact for [V47](../../V47-fury-level-one.md). Every expected value below was derived
from the pinned Steel Compendium **before** our evaluator was run, and our evaluator has not been run
on any of these builds — no test, build or browser has executed for this unit. Expected outcomes in
tests must come from the source, not from the code under test; this document is that source-derived
record.

Pins: Compendium `fb83a789da8f0327a389c277a0c790b1648d5810`, Forge Steel
`5a846aadb623a9855a023e9403bb887a956c341f`.

The five builds witness the 17 options this unit newly enables. Reused already-verified choices
(ordinary kits, the skill pool, cultures, careers, perks) are marked as reused and are not
re-witnessed. Capture procedure is in [the capture plan](capture-plan.md); test cases are in
[the test plan](test-plan.md).

## Conventions that the choice maps must respect

Established by reading the assembled definitions, not the module constants:

- `class.fury.characteristic-array` values use **U+2212 MINUS SIGN**, not a hyphen: `2, −1, −1`.
- `class.fury.array-assignment` is an object keyed `Reason`, `Intuition`, `Presence`, using each
  value of the chosen array exactly once.
- `class.fury.skills` is **one** decision of shape `multi, count 2`.
- `complication.choice` is `optional`. A build with no complication **omits the key entirely**; it
  does not supply `null` or an empty string.
- All authored text rows (`details.*`, `culture.name`, `career.what-was-taken`, `connections.notes`)
  are optional; none sets `requiredText`.
- `career.soldier.languages` is `multi, count 2, deferrable`. These builds fill both slots so every
  counterpart is a completed build.
- Every chosen skill must be distinct from every other chosen skill and from every fixed grant
  (Nature plus the aspect's skill), or the build is invalid under Q-CHAR-11.
- Careers, cultures and their child rows are regenerated by the V37 extension; the ids below are the
  ones that exist after assembly.

## Shared skeleton

All five builds share this frame so that ancestry, aspect and kit are the only moving parts. Culture
aspects are chosen so their skill pools do not collide with the class, career or ancestry picks.

| `culture.language` | `Anjali` | reused |
| `culture.environment` | `Wilderness` | pool: crafting + exploration |
| `culture.environment.skill` | `Swim` | exploration |
| `culture.organization` | `Communal` | pool: crafting + exploration |
| `culture.organization.skill` | `Blacksmithing` | crafting |
| `culture.upbringing` | `Martial` | explicit list, no pool |
| `culture.upbringing.skill` | `Intimidate` | interpersonal, from the Martial list |
| `career.choice` | `Soldier` | reused |
| `career.soldier.skill.exploration` | `Endurance` | |
| `career.soldier.skill.intrigue` | `Alertness` | |

| `career.soldier.perk` | `Teamwork` | reused |
| `career.soldier.inciting-incident` | `Sole Survivor` | |
| `class.choice` | `Fury` | |
| `class.fury.skills` | `["Climb", "Search"]` | distinct from Nature, Lift/Hide/Track, Swim, Blacksmithing, Intimidate, Endurance, Alertness |
| `complication.choice` | *omitted* | optional; the Lycanthropy exclusion is a negative test, not a build |

Culture contributes Caelian automatically plus the chosen culture language, and the career adds two
more, so every build has four languages: Caelian, Anjali, Vaslorian, Hyrallic.

## Build D — Devil Stormwight, Raden

Identical to Build C except the array, abilities and kit, so any derived difference is attributable
to the kit. Abilities reuse the already-enabled trio deliberately.

| Decision | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `class.fury.characteristic-array` | `1, 0, 0` |
| `class.fury.array-assignment` | `{ "Reason": 1, "Intuition": 0, "Presence": 0 }` |
| `class.fury.signature-ability` | `Brutal Slam` |
| `class.fury.ability-3` | `Out of the Way!` |
| `class.fury.ability-5` | `Thunder Roar` |
| `kit.choice` | `Raden` |

Expected: Stamina **24**, recovery 8, winded 12, size 1M, speed **9** (6 + 3), stability 0,
disengage **2**, melee +2/+2/+2, save 5, storm corruption, kit signature Driving Pounce. Raden's
Aspect Benefits — edge on hide and sneak tests **and ignoring difficult terrain** — are always
available, not form-conditional. Rat form adds size 1T, automatic full-speed climbing, Hide as a
free maneuver, allies as cover, staying hidden through occupied squares, an edge on tests to climb
creatures, and the same restriction to Aspect of the Wild only.

## Build E — Devil Stormwight, Vuken

Identical to Build D except the kit.

| Decision | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `kit.choice` | `Vuken` |

Expected: Stamina **30**, recovery 10, winded 15, size 1M, speed **8**, stability 0, disengage **2**,
melee +2/+2/+2, save 5, storm lightning, kit signature Unbalancing Attack.

**Vuken's two +2 speed figures.** The build speed is 8: Beast Legs sets 6, plus the unconditional kit
Speed Bonus of +2, which applies in true, animal and hybrid form. The further "+2 bonus to speed" in
the wolf and hybrid form entries is conditional on being shapeshifted, which requires using Aspect of
the Wild as a maneuver, so it is **not** part of the level-one build value. In wolf or hybrid form
the character is speed 10 and size 1L; record that as conditional, never as the base. Getting this
wrong in either direction — omitting the kit bonus or flattening the form bonus into the sheet — is
the most likely arithmetic error in this unit.

## Normalized comparison fields

A `.ds-hero` export embeds definitions as well as choices, including whole subclass trees and later
levels, so a field-by-field diff of the raw file is meaningless. Normalize both sides to this set
before comparing, and compare nothing else:

| Field | From the Forge export | From Salient |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ancestry, culture, career, class, subclass, level | the embedded objects' names and `class.level`, ignoring unselected subclass definitions, which carry their own `selected` flag | the corresponding derived values |
| Characteristics | `characteristics` | derived characteristics |
| Chosen abilities | class ability choices store `data.selectedIDs`; resolve ids to names within their owning class/subclass, since Forge ids are not globally unique | the three ability selections |
| Skills, languages | string arrays on the relevant features | derived skill and language lists |
| Kit | kit selections are arrays of objects | the kit selection and its derived contributions |
| Derived sheet values | Stamina maximum, recoveries, recovery value, winded, speed, size, stability, disengage, damage bonuses as rendered on the sheet, captured as text and screenshot | the same derived fields |
| Explicitly excluded | `state` (Stamina damage, recoveries used, surges, Victories, XP, conditions, inventory, notes), `abilityCustomizations`, pictures, folder, ids | not compared; these are play state or identity, not the build |

Compare our expectations against **both** sides. Forge agreeing with us is not evidence that either
matches the source; the source-derived column above is the arbiter, and a Forge difference needs a
recorded source-backed explanation before the unit can pass.

## Hazards recorded during derivation

1. **Kit signature abilities already include their kit's bonuses.** Chapter 6 states it directly:
   "Each kit grants a signature ability, whose distance and damage already includes the kit's
   bonuses." So Bear Claws, Wing Buffet, Driving Pounce and Unbalancing Attack must **not** have the
   kit's melee damage bonus added again, while the Fury's own chosen abilities and both free strikes
   **do** receive it. The arithmetic corroborates: the standard 2/5/7 signature progression plus
   Boren's +0/+0/+4 gives Bear Claws' printed 2/5/11, and plus Raden's +2/+2/+2 gives Driving
   Pounce's printed 4/7/9. Our existing fixtures record per-ability damage tiers, so this is a live
   risk in the expected values, not a theoretical one.
2. **Beast Legs sets speed, it does not add.** "You have speed 6." For a Devil whose baseline is 5
   the two readings coincide numerically, so these builds cannot distinguish them; keep the set
   semantics anyway, because it matters once another speed-setting effect exists.
3. **The echelon multiplier is not spelled out.** The source says a kit's Stamina bonus is "+N per
   echelon" and "scales with your echelon", and numbers the echelons, but gives no worked example
   fixing ×1 at the 1st echelon. Every value above uses ×1, which is the only reading consistent
   with the text and matches the existing merged Berserker fixture. Recorded as an interpretation,
   not presented as an explicit statement.
4. **Two potency definitions coexist.** The class entry keys potency to Might; the general rule keys
   it to the highest characteristic. Might is highest or tied in all five builds, so they agree here.
   A future fixture that makes Might not the highest would separate the two implementations; that is
   worth adding later, but it is not this unit's scope.
5. **Ancestry points are a ceiling, not a quota**, so a Polder build that spends nothing is legal on
   the source text. Build B spends all four anyway, so the reference does not depend on which
   reading a builder takes. If Forge refuses an under-spent budget, that is a structural difference
   to record, not a rules finding.
6. **Stormwight kits are kits in one place and class features in another.** The kit records carry no
   bonus figures at all — they hold only flavour and the signature ability — and the four kits are
   absent from the ordinary Kits table. Every figure lives under `feature/fury/<kit>/`. A builder
   that reads kit bonuses from the kit record produces zero bonuses for Builds B–E, which is exactly
   the failure mode our own missing contribution rows would produce.
